learningObjective: Identify when producer-consumer fusion of a pointwise op into a reduction is illegal or unprofitable due to reuse patterns.

canonicalClaims.claim: Vertical fusion of a producer with a consumer is semantics-preserving, but when the producer has multiple downstream consumers, the compiler faces a trade-off: recompute the producer inside the fused region (extra FLOPs) or keep it materialized (loses fusion's memory benefit).
conditions: Producer is not an explicit output of the graph.
nonImplications: Does not imply fusion is illegal in multi-consumer cases; only that it requires a policy choice.
Does not imply recompute is always worse than materialization.

misconceptions.claim: A shape-changing consumer (e.g., reduction) blocks fusion of a pointwise producer.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Pointwise-into-reduction is a standard fusion pattern in TVM, XLA, and TorchInductor; shape change of the output does not affect legality.

misconceptions.claim: Producer-consumer fusion is legal only when the producer function is bijective so the original tensor can be reconstructed.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Fusion inlines the producer; it does not require inverting it. Multi-consumer cases are handled by recompute or duplicate materialization.

misconceptions.claim: Fusion is always beneficial when it is legal, because it reduces memory traffic.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Register pressure, spill, reduced parallelism, or forced recomputation can make fused kernels slower than the unfused pair.

misconceptions.claim: Fusion of pointwise-into-reduction violates SSA form unless the reduction is on the last axis.
misconceptions.whyWrong: SSA governs value assignment, not loop-axis choice; reduction-axis position affects layout/coalescing, not SSA.

implementationFacts: TVM Relax fuse-ops pass classifies ops as kInjective / kReduction / kOpaque etc. and applies pattern rules.
TorchInductor scheduler keeps producers unfused when a second consumer exists and recompute cost is high.
performanceScenarios: When `f(A) = A * A` (cheap) and `T` is large, recompute-and-fuse saves HBM traffic even with duplicated FLOPs.
When `f` is expensive (e.g., softmax) and multiple consumers exist, materialize once and share.
